configuration.dataset: UMUDGA (University of Murcia Domain Generation Algorithm Dataset)
configuration.citation: Zago, Gil Perez & Martinez Perez, Computers & Security, 2020
configuration.selection: 12 of 37 eligible folders, evenly spaced across the sorted folder-id listing

expected_behavior.provenance: real malware DGA code output, not a synthetic re-implementation of a published algorithm's shape
expected_behavior.diversity: visually confirmed cross-family diversity in the 12 sampled folders -- fixed-length random-alnum, variable-length random-alnum, hex-hash-style, and two distinct dictionary-word-concatenation (Suppobox-like) shapes

applies_to_datasets: in-memory only -- train_dga.py, not persisted to a CSV (raw sample cached in training/dga_real_umudga.csv)
notes: UMUDGA's own file-listing API exposes only opaque per-family folder UUIDs, not the official malware family name -- the dataset's DOI/paper is the authoritative source for the 50-family roster. Each row here carries its real source_folder_id and a purely descriptive shape_hint (see scripts/download_umudga_dga.py), never an asserted family name. Two other candidate real-domain sources were tried and rejected first: Bambenek Consulting's feed requires a manually-issued license even for research use (not a plug-and-fetch download), and Netlab 360's feed's TLS certificate expired Dec 2023 and the host is unreachable from this environment -- both documented in the download script in case either becomes usable again.
